rows.label: Historical Agastya · conditional activity
rows.note: Working scenario: a real individual stands behind the Agastya-attributed Vedic hymns, and those attributions reflect his activity. The broad Ṛgvedic composition horizon supplies a provisional activity window only under those additional assumptions. This is neither a 500-year lifespan nor an independently established birth/death range; a historical core could also predate the surviving formulations.
rows.source: Jamison and Brereton, The Rigveda (2020) · corpus date; historical-person placement is our conditional inference

rows.label: Ṛgveda · composition horizon
rows.range: Latter half of the second millennium BCE
rows.note: Broad corpus horizon from Jamison–Brereton; not a dated birth, death, or individual hymn. Oral composition complicates finer dating.

rows.label: Mahābhārata · formative period
rows.note: Broad corpus formation, not the date of the war or the date of Agastya.
rows.source: Gregory Nagy, Homeric Questions: comparison with Sanskrit epics

rows.label: Rāmāyaṇa · formative period
rows.note: Broad scholarly model of epic formation; individual Agastya passages may have different histories. Earlier oral material and later growth are not excluded.
rows.source: Gregory Nagy, Homeric Questions: comparison with Sanskrit epics

rows.label: Bhāgavata · older alternative (Ray, 1935)
rows.note: Historical alternative in the dating literature; not represented as equal to a current consensus or as Agastya’s lifetime.
rows.source: Amarnath Ray, Bhāgavata Purāna and the Kārikās of Gaudapāda (1935)

rows.label: Bhāgavata · Holdrege’s dating
rows.note: Numeric endpoints are visualization approximations to the source’s century wording. Applies to text, not narrated persons.
rows.source: Barbara Holdrege, Mystical Cognition and Canonical Authority (2000)

rows.label: Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar · commentary witness
rows.note: Dates this witness to the disciple tradition, not the origin of every Tamil Agastya tradition and not the life of Tolkāppiyar or Agastya.
rows.source: Kamil Zvelebil, Pre-history of Tamil Literature

assumption: A historical core behind Vedic Agastya attributions; later texts are witnesses to the tradition, not additions to one lifespan.
